chunks: Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Ḥabīb ibn Muẓāhir, who said:

I began the obligatory tawaf and completed one round, when suddenly a person struck my nose and made it bleed. So I went out and washed it, then came back and began the tawaf again. Then I mentioned that to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
So he said: “What you did was bad; you should have built upon what you had already circled.” Then he said: “Indeed, there is nothing upon you.”

key_terms.تَبْنِيَ عَلَى مَا طُفْتَ: to continue from the point already completed in tawaf
key_terms.طَوَافِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory tawaf being performed as a required rite
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ شَيْءٌ: there is no liability, penalty, or expiation upon you

ai.seo_question: If my obligatory tawaf is interrupted by bleeding, should I restart it or continue from where I stopped?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about an interruption during the obligatory tawaf. If a person leaves briefly due to an incident such as bleeding, he should resume from where he stopped rather than restart the tawaf, though in this case no penalty was due.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2798 - Hammad ibn Uthman narrated from Habib ibn Muzahir, who said:

I began the obligatory tawaf and completed one round when someone hit my nose, causing it to bleed. I left, washed it, and then returned to start the tawaf over. I mentioned this to Abu Abdullah (as).
Imam (as) said: "What you did was not correct. You should have continued from where you left off. However, there is no penalty upon you."
